blocks.text: CHOSEN: THE STORY BEFORE THE MANGER
Let the audience stay with her happiness.
Mary looks toward the place Joseph exited.
She begins quietly putting things in order.
straightens the unfinished table piece Joseph showed her;
touches the wood and imagines the future they were just discussing.
The distant sounds of Nazareth are still present.
Something completely different from the musical language of Nazareth.
Gabriel does not rush toward her.
Stillness is part of the power of the moment.
You have found favor with God.
Still walks away from Gabriel slowly
Still walks backwards away from Gabriel
Still walks backwards away from Gabriel
I have been sent by God.
She looks toward the doorway, as though part of her still expects someone else to walk in and make this ordinary again.
Her mind simply cannot make the words fit.
What will happen comes from God.
I don't understand how they can be true.
Nothing God has spoken is beyond His power.
It may be the only answer you are given tonight.
You expect me to believe this?
I expect you to decide whether you will trust the One who sent me.
Your relative Elizabeth is also expecting a child.
She knows what she was going to say.
This is the first piece of the message she can attach to something in her world.
Go to her if you need to see what God has already begun.
Mary looks toward the unfinished table.
The future from Scene 2 is sitting in front of her.
What am I supposed to tell Joseph?
And if the truth sounds impossible?
It will still be the truth.
That doesn't mean he'll believe me.
That is not the answer she wanted.
Her eyes move back to the table.
He thinks he knows how our life is supposed to go.
He remains present, but the focus begins transferring to Mary.
The song begins because she has finally understood
I knew the road to the well,
I knew the shape of the day,
I knew the life I was promised
BLOCKING: Mary stays where the dialogue leaves her, near the unfinished table. Do not move into a new “song position.”
I knew the voice of my mother,
I knew the work of my hands,
I knew the quiet kind of future
A girl like me could plan.
BLOCKING: On “the future,” touch or straighten the unfinished table. Let it represent the home, marriage, and life Mary expected. Gabriel stays grounded and mostly still.
Then the air begins to tremble,
Then the light begins to rise,
BLOCKING: Mary looks back to Gabriel. The room she knows now feels unfamiliar. Gabriel does not chase or circle her.
BLOCKING: Mary takes one instinctive step toward the exit or away from Gabriel, then stops herself.
BLOCKING: Mary turns back toward Gabriel. Keep the movement simple.
I don’t know where this road will lead,
BLOCKING: Mary moves only slightly downstage into open space. She is testing the word “chosen,” not celebrating it.
Can heaven ask these hands of mine
To hold what I can’t name?
BLOCKING: On “these hands of mine,” one brief look at her hands is enough.
BLOCKING: Stop moving. Let the question hang.
When he looks into my eyes?
Will he hear the truth in me,
BLOCKING: Mary moves toward the place Joseph exited, but does not leave.
When the whispers start to grow?
When no one else can know?
BLOCKING: Become aware of the village outside the room. Do not mime people gossiping.
I thought faith was something steady,
Like a lamp beside the door.
Now it feels like stepping forward
BLOCKING: Mary shifts her weight forward and begins the idea of a step, but stops before fully taking it. She wants to move, but fear still holds her.
BLOCKING: Stay grounded. Let the questions work on Mary instead of adding more movement.
I don’t know what this yes will cost,
BLOCKING: On “what this yes will cost,” look back at the unfinished table, but do not return to it.
Can mercy ask a life like mine
BLOCKING: Mary is still frightened, but she no longer retreats.
BLOCKING: Mary returns to the unfinished table. Place the cloth or simple object she has been holding onto the table.
BLOCKING: Remove her hand from the table. This is a quiet release, not a dramatic gesture.
Then I will take it trembling,
But I will not walk alone.
BLOCKING: Mary now completes the step she could not take earlier. One deliberate step forward. She still cannot see the road, but now she chooses to move.
Not because I know the plan.
BLOCKING: Mary becomes steady, not triumphant. Use very little movement.
But if You are the One who calls me,
I will trust the One who knows.
Still my answer will be Yours.
BLOCKING: On “Let the world misunderstand me,” briefly acknowledge the village outside. On “Still my answer will be Yours,” return focus to Gabriel.
BLOCKING: Hold still on “But I am willing.” This is the emotional peak. No heroic pose or giant finish.
Let it be as You have spoken.

BLOCKING: Let the music settle. No victory pose. In the song, Mary makes the decision privately within herself. The spoken acceptance that follows is when she gives that decision to Gabriel — her final “yes.”
THE MUSIC APPROACHES ITS FINAL RESOLUTION
I don't understand what comes next.
But if God has asked this of me...
Let it be with me as He has said.
Let the decision stand by itself.
For the first time, there may be something almost tender in his expression.
The light around Gabriel begins to change.
Do not make his departure a magic trick simply for spectacle.
Mary's attention being pulled briefly elsewhere and finding him gone.
A faint fragment of “My Beloved” is heard.
Not because she regrets saying yes.
Because now she understands what she has to do next.
She looks toward the direction Joseph left.

NEAR-BLACK TRANSITION INTO SCENE 4: Hold a narrow special on Mary after “Joseph...” for one breath. Fade the surrounding stage and LED to deep blue near-black. Keep Mary's side exit path safely lit as she leaves. The unfinished table stays in place; the friends' small work props are preset. No furniture moves in darkness. Bring up ordinary daylight on the friends' work area.

Mary begins in the emotional afterglow of Scene 2, Gabriel’s arrival interrupts rather than overwhelms the world, the dialogue carries the revelation and Mary’s questions, and “Chosen” begins only when Mary understands the personal cost of saying yes. This scene is about Mary’s calling
